data.name: Azael
data.gender_notes: Azael is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Azael means 'God is helper' in Hebrew. In the Bible, Azael is a name of an angel and a demon. As an angel, Azael was responsible for caring for animals and nature. As a demon, he was believed to be the ruler of all demons, the ‘Satan of Satans.’. The name Azael carries the meaning “God is helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Azael usually hope their child will grow to embody god is helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine assistance and protection.
data.etymology: Azael belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Azael total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: עזאזל
in_hebrew.meaning: עזאזל - השם שמייחס לאלוהים, נושא עוון, או שד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עזאזל הוא שם שמקורו בתנ"ך העברי, ומוזכר בספר ויקרא ובספר דברי הימים. הוא מתייחס לשד או לנושא עוון ששוחרר ביום כ赎תיים, לפי המשמעות המסורתית. העובדה שזהו אחד משמות ה'שדים' או ישויות הרע בתפיסה היהודית, מאשרת את המשמעות הרעיונית הקשורה לשם זה. השם עצמו בנוי משתי מילים: עזאז, שיכול להתפרש כ'חזק' או 'עז', ו־אל, שפירושו 'אלוהים' או 'אל'. לכן, עזאזל יכול להתפרש כ'אלוהים החזק' או 'עוז אלוהים', אך בהקשר התנ"כי הוא קשור יותר לנושא עוון.

in_greek.name: Αζαήλ
in_greek.meaning: Αζαήλ - το όνομα που σχετίζεται με το Θεό, ο φορέας της αμαρτίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Αζαήλ είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή Αγία Γραφή και αναφέρεται στο βιβλίο του Λευιτικού και στο βιβλίο των Χρονικών. Αναφέρεται σε δαιμόνιο ή φορέα αμαρτίας που απελευθερώνεται την Ημέρα της Εξιλέωσης, σύμφωνα με την παραδοσιακή ερμηνεία. Το ίδιο το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: Αζαζ, που μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'ισχυρός' ή 'ελεύθερος', και -ήλ, που σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Έτσι, το Αζαήλ μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'Ισχυρός Θεός' ή 'Θεός της δύναμης', αλλά στο πλαίσιο της Αγίας Γραφής συνδέεται περισσότερο με τον φορέα της αμαρτίας.

in_latin.name: Azael
in_latin.meaning: Azael - nomen Dei, portator peccati, daemon
in_latin.long_meaning: Azael est nomen origine Hebraicae Scripturae, in libro Levitici et libro Chronicorum memoratum. Refertur ad daemonium vel portatorem peccati qui die Expiationis dimittebatur, iuxta interpretationem traditionalem. Nomen ipsum ex duabus vocibus constat: Azaz, quod interpretari potest 'fortis' vel 'liber', et -ael, quod significat 'Deus'. Ita Azael interpretari potest 'Deus fortis' vel 'Dei fortitudo', sed in contextu Scripturae sacrae magis coniungitur cum portatore peccati.

in_english.name: Azael
in_english.meaning: Azael - God strengthens, bearer of sin, or demon
in_english.long_meaning: Azael originates from the Hebrew Bible, mentioned in Leviticus and Chronicles. Traditionally, it refers to a demon or a scapegoat released on Yom Kippur. Etymologically, it combines 'Azaz', meaning 'strong' or 'free', and 'El', meaning 'God'. Hence, Azael can be interpreted as 'God's strength' or 'strong God', but in Christian tradition, it's associated with a bearer of sin or an entity representing evil.

data.cultural_impact: The name Azael has cultural significance in Jewish and Christian folklore. In Jewish tradition, the name Azael is associated with the biblical figure Azazel, who was believed to be the angel of destruction and chaos. In Christian mythology, Azael is depicted as a fallen angel, a demon who tempted Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden and led humanity away from God. This cultural significance can be seen in various artistic and literary works throughout history, from medieval illuminated manuscripts to modern novels and films.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Azael holds deep spiritual significance as a reminder of both the divine help and the potential for destruction in the world. The name 'God is helper' reflects the belief in the presence and power of God in the world and in our lives, providing comfort and strength in times of need. However, as Azael is also associated with the temptation and fall from grace, the name represents the importance of choosing the right path and staying true to our faith. In this way, Azael can be seen as a symbol of the ongoing spiritual battle between good and evil, and a reminder of the power of God's help and guidance to overcome even the greatest challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Azael, meaning "whom God has helped," is a name that symbolizes divine assistance and protection. It is a reminder that even in the darkest moments, God is present, offering strength and hope.

biblical_reference.note: Scapegoat or demon released on Yom Kippur

historical_references.reference: In the apocryphal Book of Enoch, there is a mention of a fallen angel named Azael who fathered giants with human women after the Deluge.
historical_references.context: The Book of Enoch is an ancient Jewish text, ascribed to the prophet Enoch and considered non-canonical by most Jewish and Christian traditions. It describes a series of visions granted to Enoch, which include various teachings and angels, the history of the world, and the coming of the Messiah.

historical_references.reference: In the medieval Jewish and Christian mystical tradition, Azael is believed to be the Angel of Death, the one who separates the soul from the body at the moment of death.
historical_references.context: The belief in Azael as the Angel of Death is derived from various mystical texts, including the Zohar, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism, and the writings of Christian mystics such as Meister Eckhart and Jacob Boehme. In this context, Azael is seen as a powerful and feared figure, responsible for the ultimate separation of the soul from the body.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the Christian name Azael is most commonly found in the contexts of angelology, gaming, and fantasy literature. In tabletop RPGs, Azael is often portrayed as a powerful and enigmatic fallen angel, tempting or tormenting the player characters. In video games, Azael is the name of an enemy or boss in various titles, representing destructive or malevolent forces. In fantasy literature, Azael is a character or a reference to a character, often as a fallen angel or demon. This usage of the name reflects the enduring fascination with angelic lore and the supernatural in modern popular culture.
